title: Assets bought before 1985 lose their CGT-free status
headline: Assets bought before 20 September 1985 become taxable on growth after 1 July 2027. Growth up to then stays tax-free.
summary: Pre-CGT assets have been exempt from capital gains tax since CGT began in 1985. From 1 July 2027 they are treated as sold and reacquired at market value, so only growth after that date is taxed, under the new indexation rules.
effectiveLabel: CGT events on or after 1 July 2027

history.note: Treasury Laws Amendment (Tax Reform No. 1) Act 2026

bigStat.caption: assets bought before 20 September 1985 lose their exemption

before: Assets acquired before 20 September 1985 were permanently exempt from capital gains tax.
after: Pre-1985 assets held on 30 June 2027 are treated as sold and reacquired at market value just before 1 July 2027.
Growth up to that date stays tax-free. Growth after it is taxed under the indexation rules, with the 30% minimum for individuals.
It applies to every kind of owner, including companies.

workedExample.title: Explanatory Memorandum example: Eileen
steps: Eileen's pre-1985 asset is worth $1 million at 30 June 2027.
She sells it in 2030 for $1.5 million.
workedExample.result: She is taxed on $1.5 million less her $1 million cost base indexed for inflation since July 2027. All the growth before July 2027 stays exempt.

actions.text: Plan for evidence of each pre-1985 asset's market value just before 1 July 2027: a valuation as at that date, or the quoted price for listed shares.

positions.summary: Part of the CGT reform legislated in June 2026.
Pledges to reverse Labor's changes to capital gains tax. It has not said specifically what it would do about pre-1985 assets.
